creator: alanonai
title: Engineering for Vibe Coders: an emailed 6-digit code is not real MFA (email+password+code are all 'something you know'); true MFA is a lifecycle (lost phone, deleted authenticator, impersonation on support calls, reset flow)

tools.name: Engineering for Vibe Coders (article series)
tools.detail: Creator's own written series; MFA article link 'in the comments' (URL not shown)

claims: A six-digit code emailed at login is NOT multi-factor authentication: email address, password and emailed code are all 'something you know' (same factor)
The three factors are something you know, something you have (phone), something you are (biometrics); MFA needs at least two different factors
MFA is 'an entire system and life cycle', not a checkbox: must design for lost/new phone, deleted authenticator app, callers claiming to be the user, password/MFA reset verification
how_to_steps: Audit your login: if the second step is an emailed code, you have one factor, not two
Pick a second factor from a different category (TOTP authenticator app or passkey = something you have; biometric = something you are)
Design the recovery lifecycle: lost/new phone, deleted authenticator app, support impersonation, how you verify identity before resetting password or MFA
Read the creator's MFA article (link in comments) for the full checklist
on_screen_only: Only burned-in captions of the spoken words (e.g. 'THE FOCUS IS ON THE WORD FACTOR, NOT THE WORD MULTI', 'IT'S AN ENTIRE SYSTEM AND LIFE CYCLE')
No URLs, code or UI shown; creator talking outdoors in a 'rage against the machine learning' t-shirt
cta: Link to the article in the comments; 'let me know if this is helpful'

relevance.why: Directly fixes a mistake Claude-built auth commonly makes (email OTP marketed as MFA). Veteran-facing apps that handle VA/PII data need correct auth; the recovery-lifecycle framing is the part solo founders skip.

implement_score.why: Cheap to act on: ask Claude Code to audit the auth flow against the three-factor rule and add TOTP/passkeys via the auth provider (Supabase/Clerk/Auth.js all support it), then write the recovery flow (backup codes, re-verification before MFA reset). Half a day per app.

verify: Find the actual article URL in the comments and check it covers recovery/backup codes
Confirm which second factor the app's auth provider supports natively (TOTP, passkeys/WebAuthn) to avoid hand-rolling MFA
Is email OTP acceptable as a step-up for low-risk apps even if not 'true' MFA? Decide per app risk level

gap.what: The liked set covers login gaps (no email verification, rate limiting, unhashed passwords) and authN vs authZ, but not the 'email OTP is not a second factor' correction or the MFA recovery lifecycle (lost phone, support impersonation). This is a specific correction, from the same creator whose Supabase/Vercel videos Haji liked.
